question.prompt: The sum of two natural numbers is \(17{,}402.\) One of the two numbers is divisible by \(10.\) If the units digit of that number is erased, the other number is obtained. What is the difference of these two numbers?

solutions.explanation:
Erasing the final zero divides a number by \(10\). If the smaller number is \(n\), the larger is therefore \(10n\).

Their sum gives \(11n=17{,}402\), so \(n=1582\). Their difference is
\[
10n-n=9n=9\cdot1582=\boxed{14{,}238},
\]
choice D. Interpret deleting a digit as an operation on place value before setting up the equation.
solutions.title: Translate deletion of a trailing zero into a tenfold relation.
